summary: Get attachment for project asset type
description: Gets a specific project-scoped asset type attachment by ID

parameters.name: asset_type_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the Asset Type

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Locale for localized response messages (for example: en, fr-FR, pseudo)

file_download_url.description: Download URL for the attachment. Only populated when fetching a single attachment by ID or via bulk attachment APIs

asset_id.description: Asset ID this attachment belongs to. Only populated in bulk attachment list responses.

asset_code.description: Asset code this attachment belongs to. Only populated in bulk attachment list responses.

asset_type_id.description: Asset type ID when this attachment is stored at asset type scope (row has asset_type_id). Omitted for asset-only attachments.

attachment_level.description: Scope at which this attachment row lives in the database: COMPANY_ASSET (asset-level, no project), PROJECT_ASSET (asset-level, project), COMPANY_ASSET_TYPE (type-level, no project), PROJECT_ASSET_T...

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.
